audit_scope.description: Auditing EL gas economics (blob gas, ModExp pricing), EL-CL fork activation coordination, P2P fork digest rotation, and JSON-RPC gas cap query. Both EL and CL are materially involved.

out_of_scope: JSON-RPC API general endpoints (out-of-scope per bug bounty)

out_of_scope_reasons.Mainnet/Testnet Testing: All testing should be done on local forks
out_of_scope_reasons.Pricing Oracles (Third-party): Incorrect data from third-party oracles out-of-scope (oracle manipulation/flash loan attacks ARE in-scope)
out_of_scope_reasons.Privileged Access: Impacts requiring privileged address access without additional modifications are out-of-scope
out_of_scope_reasons.Centralization Risks: Impacts involving centralization risks are out-of-scope
out_of_scope_reasons.Known Issues: Known issues from previous audits are out-of-scope

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip network (ENR discovery, gossip topic subscription)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes on the P2P network are unauthenticated. Any node can advertise ENR records and subscribe to gossip topics. Malicious peers could advertise stale fork digests or fail to rotate topics, causing network partitioning.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethereum RPC Node via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RPC node responds to client queries. From the wallet/client perspective, the node is untrusted — it could return incorrect gas cap values. From the node perspective, RPC requests from clients are unauthenticated user input.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via Wallet/JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction submission via eth_sendRawTransaction and gas cap queries
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users interact via wallets over JSON-RPC. No authentication required. Users may submit malformed or adversarial transactions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contract / EOA via EVM CALL
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: CALL to ModExp precompile at address 0x05
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any smart contract or EOA can invoke the ModExp precompile with arbitrary input data. Inputs are fully attacker-controlled and could be crafted to maximize computation relative to gas cost.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (newPayload, forkchoiceUpdated) for fork activation coordination
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL communicates with EL over authenticated JWT channel (Engine API). Channel is authenticated but payload content (e.g., fork activation signals, blob parameters) must still be validated by EL.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via CL P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators propose blocks and submit attestations over the P2P network. A malicious validator could propose blocks with incorrect blob parameters after a BPO fork, or submit conflicting attestations.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P gossip topic subscription and ENR discovery
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Node must validate fork digest values in ENR records. Must handle peers advertising stale or incorrect fork digests without crashing or partitioning. Must validate all gossip messages against current fork rules.
Node must compute gas cap correctly from protocol and policy parameters. Clients consuming this data should not blindly trust the response — must handle null and unexpected values gracefully.
Full transaction validation required including gas limit checks, signature verification, nonce validation, and blob gas fee validation per EIP-7892 parameters.

Gas pricing must accurately reflect computational cost per EIP-7883 formula. Input parsing must handle malformed calldata (truncated lengths, oversized values) without panics or excessive resource consumption. The 500 gas floor must be enforced.

EL must independently validate fork activation timestamps against its own blob schedule configuration. Must not blindly accept CL-provided fork parameters without cross-checking against local config. JWT authentication must be verified.

CL must validate proposed blocks against current fork rules including correct blob parameters post-BPO fork. Must reject blocks with blob counts exceeding MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK for the active schedule entry.
